exposure: Timing of IUC insertion (immediate postpartum vs delayed postpartum)
Mode of delivery (vaginal vs Caesarean section)
outcome: Effect on sexual health and general well-being
finding: Intrauterine contraceptives (IUCs) are a highly effective, safe, and cost-effective method of contraception with several non-contraceptive benefits, including decreased menstrual blood loss, dysmenorrhea, and risk of endometrial cancer
mod_finding: Immediate insertion of an IUC postpartum (10 minutes postplacental to 48 hours) or post-Caesarean section is associated with a higher continuation rate compared with insertion at 6 weeks postpartum, but also with a higher risk of expulsion; however, the benefits of immediate insertion outweigh the risks
